displayQuote: Education is the passport to the future

meta.title: Who really said "Education is the passport to the future"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Yes — Malcolm X said it, at the OAAU founding rally on 28 June 1964. But his words were “our passport… the people who prepare,” not the popular “the passport… those who prepare.”
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Education is the passport to the future'?
meta.ogDescription: Malcolm X did say it — 28 June 1964, OAAU founding rally. His authentic words: “our passport… the people who prepare for it today.”

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: Malcolm X delivered this line on 28 June 1964, reading the Organization of Afro-American Unity’s statement of aims at the group’s founding rally in Harlem’s Audubon Ballroom — a speech later published in By Any Means Necessary (1970). His documented words were “Education is our passport to the future, for tomorrow belongs only to the people who prepare for it today.” The much-shared “the passport … those who prepare for it today” is a genuine but slightly reworded paraphrase of that line.

docMeta.dd: Founding Rally of the Organization of Afro-American Unity

source.excerpt: Education is an important element in the struggle for human rights. It is the means to help our children and our people rediscover their identity and thereby increase their self-respect. Education is our passport to the future, for tomorrow belongs only to the people who prepare for it today.
trail: The line traces to Malcolm X’s speech at the OAAU founding rally, 28 June 1964, where he read the group’s statement of aims aloud.
An independent transcript of the same speech confirms the wording verbatim: “Education is our passport to the future, for tomorrow belongs only to the people who prepare for it today.”
The speech was later collected in By Any Means Necessary (New York: Pathfinder Press, 1970), the standard published source for it.
Popular quote sites circulate an altered short form — e.g. “the passport … those who prepare for it today” — swapping “our” for “the” and dropping “only.”
source.excerptNote: From Section III (“Education”) of the OAAU statement of aims, which Malcolm X read aloud at the founding rally.

author.name: Malcolm X
author.heading: About Malcolm X
author.bio: Malcolm X (born Malcolm Little; also El-Hajj Malik El-Shabazz, 1925–1965) was an American Muslim minister and one of the most influential voices of the Black freedom movement. After breaking with the Nation of Islam in 1964 he founded the Organization of Afro-American Unity, whose statement of aims placed education at the center of the struggle for human rights. He was assassinated in February 1965.

items.why: His documented words at the OAAU founding rally were “Education is our passport to the future, for tomorrow belongs only to the people who prepare for it today” (full transcript). The popular short form swaps “our” for “the,” “the people” for “those,” and drops “only.”

misattribution.truthLine: Bottom line: Malcolm X really said it — on 28 June 1964 — but his exact words were “Education is our passport to the future … the people who prepare for it today.”

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: When Malcolm X founded the Organization of Afro-American Unity in June 1964, its statement of aims made education a pillar of the human-rights struggle — a tool to help Black Americans “rediscover their identity” and build self-respect. The “passport to the future” line closes that education section.

Read in context it is not a generic motivational slogan but part of a concrete program: the OAAU statement went on to demand community control of Harlem’s schools and greater parent involvement, framing education as collective self-determination rather than individual advancement.
